cases.invariant: Probes never allocate a VM; an expected missing binding is unavailable, not silently not-applicable.
A fast complete return cannot be overwritten by a later admission receipt.
Current scope, target and deadline are required for fresh evidence; unknown transport never authorizes resource recovery.
Pending observations cannot survive Projector ownership reset as fresh acknowledgements.
Partial inventory or failed guest responses cannot authorize VM destruction or quota release.
Every due physical runtime is examined without a 16-item truncation or unbounded concurrent requests.
Missing guest replies do not block publication, native drain or future log-path probes; replaced bindings reject late evidence.
At most one probe is outstanding per physical Session; a probe has no semantic commit to recover.
A pending machine release wins over a stale target lookup; rebinding checks a fresh snapshot after the machine lock.
Binding replay cannot duplicate or retarget the operation; native Session/model identity and previously accepted Run snapshots remain unchanged.
A stalled remote stop cannot stall lease scanning; drain prevents another cleanup claim.
Both initial expiry selection and final retirement use PG time, independent of API clock skew.
A replay or stale probe cannot refresh liveness or create an active execution scope.
Tenant, partition and owner checks fence phase observations; a writer seal closes all sibling observations.
Transient activity cannot alter transcript sequence or reopen a terminal turn.
Expired drafts release image pins; a revoked upload cannot become a ready input after a late external reply.
Binary upload admission is bounded before buffering; image pinning cannot acknowledge a GC-deleted source.
Upload placement cannot follow a substituted directory or destination link outside the authorized root.
Input preparation is fenced independently of Agent Tool execution and remains tracked until guest cancellation finishes.
Expiring a child's independent compute scope keeps the shared Volume and the active parent's runtime; each binding uses its own frozen cwd.
Cancellation revokes Tool authority before uncertain process cleanup returns.
Loss of one Workspace Cube cannot leave a surviving logical Tool binding.
Broker shutdown rejects pending VM creation before freeing existing capacity; it never launches the waiter during teardown.
A proved pre-enqueue rejection restores committed state and preserves sibling publication and contiguous sequence.
Cancellation while waiting for the Session writer neither publishes the invocation nor consumes a native sequence.
Cancelling a cold history waiter does not cancel the shared progress read or a sibling.
Previously observed progress cannot authorize a retired owner or cache a failed read.
Server lock timeout leaves native history and projection positions unchanged; redelivery after release applies once.
A timed-out SQL statement rolls back preceding writes and transaction-local timeout settings.
Final admission checks current PG time after locks; an expired lease cannot start the Agent or leave partial owner state.
Cancellation lifecycle locks remain compatible with the native Record's Turn foreign key, so neither side deadlocks.
A certified cancellation-settlement SQL abort retries only that transaction, never the external stop or Agent Loop.
A failed seal commit cannot release the next Lane task or decrement the family count; replay decrements once.
Input acceptance and seal projection serialize on the Lane row and cannot leave a committed follow-up permanently waiting.
Input waiting behind a seal transaction observes the committed closure and becomes ready without another notification.
A lost PG COMMIT reply preserves the first recovery floor and idempotent native projection.
First native data and its recovery floor roll back together, and retry cannot skip the prefix.
A blocked delivery in one partition does not serialize unrelated partition handlers.
Native intent projects before effect admission; replay never reissues the combined command.
Failed native projection cannot commit or dispatch its Tool command.
An unconfirmed Kafka dispatch commit cannot issue a Tool effect.
Lost partition ownership after commit does not dispatch a new effect.
An invocation after its scope seal cannot dispatch a Tool command.
Seal projection replay cannot duplicate a terminal or repeat execution closure; closure precedes publication.
A no-longer-current consumer handler cannot continue live or Tool delivery after its pending PG operation completes.
Accepted late native input continues within the same operation before successful Run closure.
Waiting for final durable append cannot reopen control-input admission.
A successful sampling response resets retry state before a subsequent input's sampling.
A retained pre-compaction usage value cannot force another threshold compaction.
Run cancellation interrupts retry backoff without another model call or shared-authority revocation.
Local pending reservations bound overlapping claims without a PG slot counter; successors still wait for closure.
A ready main Lane cannot acquire a new owner until the old sibling's final seal commits.
Committed text leaves live memory before the Run ends; an unfinished suffix remains exact after failure.
Kafka redelivery creates one canonical Pi Session mutation.
A replacement Worker observes every older accepted Session mutation before reading context.
A replacement Projector reconstructs the unsealed prefix without repeating native mutations.
A partial snapshot never appears in the browser or leaks into the replacement snapshot.
Duplicate delivery does not execute one Agent command twice.
A released task cannot reuse its execution reference under a retired Session owner.
A record cannot install its own authority or bypass the PG-issued publication scope.
Oversized individual publications fail before entering the bounded publication queue.
Ingress closes old admission before draining and a successor cannot pass the ordered seal.
A delayed PG grant cannot reopen a scope after its closure completed.
Unknown semantic commit stops queued data while preserving ordered closure.
PG canonical seal evidence releases a successor despite a lost producer ACK.
A live-stream failure cannot roll back a complete native Pi message.
The native Harness persists a result-size Tool error and can finish the next model Step normally.
A browser-visible interrupted prefix remains model-visible after Worker replacement.
Terminal projection unloads shared live-tail memory without invalidating an in-flight browser snapshot.
Control Plane process replacement does not revoke a healthy Agent Loop.
A stale Worker Control Channel cannot reclaim current ownership.
A Control Plane failure before provisioning cannot leak a requested development machine.
A replacement Sandbox control fences the expired owner before serving its Workspace runtime.
An ambiguous Tool transport never blindly replays an arbitrary command.
Durable binding closure rejects late Tool handoffs even after stopping is unconfirmed and the dispatcher is replaced.
Workspace bytes are not deleted while a live Cube still owns the Volume.
A Tool command cannot dispatch until Kafka confirms its monotonic commit boundary.
Rebuilding volatile display state does not replay already committed Tool commands.
Completing guest work after closure cannot publish a usable native Tool result.
Image cleanup mutates only the tenant/object identities it locked, preserving another tenant's unexpired object.
Failed uploads cannot be retained; cleanup claims survive remote deletion failure.
Kafka-acknowledged but unprojected images remain protected by their unsealed source Run.
A deleting attachment cannot gain a canonical native reference.
A hash or tenant mismatch never becomes a successful native image.
Cold reads and independent native Fork history retain the exact image bytes.
Failed publication retires the pending image-adapter callback without crashing unrelated Worker families.
Early reply rejection stays observed until command publication settles and never triggers an effect replay.
Observation-only progress cannot enter the final-result Kafka transport.
A replacement Worker cannot attach an old operation's replies to a new Tool call.
Existing adopted machines count against a lowered capacity; new work remains queued until a physical slot is free.
Provider HTTP holds no business transaction or row lock; one current note-sync claim does not block claim changes or ordinary Run admission.
An uncertain remote create remains pending; marker readback recovers the applied note without repeating its creation in the tested lost-reply case.
Local claim fencing rejects a stale acknowledgement, and periodic remote verification repairs its late external write even after PG considered the latest version synced.
Synchronization acknowledgement uses PG decision time after locking; a lease that expires while waiting cannot confirm remote output.
An admitted/locked Run cannot have its input rewritten by a pending edit.
Pending cancellation cannot retire a Run whose admission already won.
A locked queue neighbor cannot be reordered under an active admission.
Canonical input consumption resolves a lost HTTP reply without executing the queued source.
A missing reply alone cannot restore a queued source; an absent input plus projected seal can.
Promotions to the same target preserve accepted delivery order across replicas.
Shutdown starts no further deliveries and restart finds the remaining durable controls.
Concurrent API replicas cannot repeat a queue operation or silently overwrite a stale edit.
A Worker acknowledgement never retires input; target closure restores unconsumed input without replaying its Run.
Canonical input evidence wins over missing transport acknowledgement and prevents fallback execution.
A late Worker reply cannot overwrite a sealed-target restoration decision.
Stopping the active Run retains unconsumed direct input and leaves its restored queue entry removable.
Direct Steer acceptance is atomic and idempotent under target locks and concurrent API replicas.
A completed oversized workflow return becomes an explicit bounded error without repeating effects.
An older lookup cannot revoke ownership confirmed by a newer committed renewal.
Sharing heartbeat evidence does not slow periodic PG revocation observation.
Missing renewal retires the reported family while retaining other families; later replies cannot revive it.
A failed batch read fails closed for every owner in that observation.
Closing a lease observer prevents stale reads from affecting a later local incarnation.
An unsettled Session prevents schema cutover; settled cutover retains immutable bodies and never resurrects deleted Turn bindings.
Native open-operation references share the log transaction, preserve Lane/tenant scope and rebuild without re-executing effects.
Input acceptance does not deadlock with active Tool binding foreign-key checks.
